board: RF-Power-Monitor rev2: RP2040 + W5500 + WIZPoE-P1 PoE module, isolated 230 VAC mains detector, TMP1075; 100 x 64 mm, 2 layers, JLCPCB
title: RF-Power-Monitor rev2
loadsNote: VSYS 0.6 A covers USB-powered bench use with margin (calcs: 0.13 A typical); 3V3 design load 0.3 A

U3.note: W5500 at 100 Mbit/s transmitting: 132 mA x 3.3 V (datasheet 5.4); LQFP-48, no exposed pad

U4.note: RP2040 ~30 mA x 3.3 V; exposed pad is GND

pours.name: GND pour, both layers (net-class rules keep it 6.5 mm off mains and 2 mm off the PoE side)

notPouredNote: mains and PoE (MDI) nets are isolated domains: tracks only, no pour
isolationDomainsNote: KiCad rules: mains 6.5 mm clearance / 6.4 mm creepage, PoE 2.0 mm; +0.1 mm for the router's grid
hotNote: Rise budgets from each part's ratings at up to 40 C enclosure ambient: W5500 Tj 125 C max (datasheet 5.1) -> 85 C rise, budget 70; TLV62569 Tj 125 C operating -> budget 60; RP2040 85 C ambient rating -> budget 45

J2.reason: Reviewed with the owner 2026-11-03: the RJ45 sticks out over the left edge to pass through the case wall, as rev1's module jack did (4.8 mm). This jack's 3.2 mm board-lock holes allow 3.37 mm (0.5 mm of board beside them): the jack front is 3.1 mm and its courtyard 3.30 mm past the straight edge x=100, every pad inside the board.
